title: On the Fragility of Tasks under Composition: Implicit Budgeting in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.27190v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern language models are increasingly asked to handle several tasks within a single prompt. Doing so requires solving each task correctly while integrating the resulting answers into a coherent response. In this paper, we identify a fundamental limitation in this process, where models make substantially more errors when tasks are composed, even when they can solve every constituent task reliably in isolation. This degradation cannot be fully explained by the accumulation of independent errors. Across both open-weight models and the frontier model Claude Opus 5, our findings instead point to an implicit thinking budget underlying this effect. In particular, under composition, models use substantially fewer tokens per task than in isolation, even when the full sequence remains well within the context window. translated_title: 论任务组合下的脆弱性：语言模型中的隐式预算分配
translated_abstract: 现代语言模型越来越多地被要求在单个提示中处理多个任务。这需要模型正确解决每个任务，同时将各任务的结果整合成一个连贯的回复。本文识别了这一过程中的一个根本性局限：当任务被组合在一起时，模型会犯下多得多的错误，即使它们能够可靠地独立完成每一个组成任务。这种性能退化无法完全用独立错误的累积来解释。通过对开放权重模型以及前沿模型 Claude Opus 5 的研究，我们的发现指向了这一现象背后的一种隐式思考预算。具体而言，在任务组合的情况下，模型在每个任务上使用的 token 数量远少于单独处理时，即使完整序列仍远在上下文窗口范围之内。因此，那些单独求解时需要更长推理链条的任务在组合情况下会更加“脆弱”，即模型……
tldr: 语言模型存在一种隐式思考预算：在组合多个任务时，每个任务分配到的 token 数远少于单独处理时，导致即使模型能独立可靠地完成每个任务，组合后错误率仍显著上升，且需要长推理链的任务在组合下尤为脆弱。
en_tdlr: Language models exhibit an implicit thinking budget under task composition—allocating far fewer tokens per task than in isolation—leading to substantially more errors even when each task is solved reliably alone, with tasks requiring longer solution traces being the most fragile.
